chapter: Building McShann's big band and blues records
title: Walter Brown and the blues singers of Kansas City
summary: Brown was a stranger to the band; local blues singers imitated Rushing and Turner, and McShann had used ballad singers.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Yeah, while we got the motor running, let it keep on running.
What were we talking about last --
I just remember, one of the last things I said was in reference to Frank Sinatra, but --

Yeah. And comparing him with others. [Walter Brown] But somebody said he was born and raised in Dallas, Texas, and they say he died there. Somewhere near the same time that -- no, I think somebody said he died rather recently.

Maybe four or five years ago. But Brown was, like, he was a total stranger to us. I don't know how or when or where Mashann got him, Johnny Tumino got him or who got him. We had quite a few blues singers around Kansas City by that time, but they all to us seemed like they were poor imitations of Jimmy Rushing and George Turner.
So we didn't pay any attention to them, in fact, all the time previously McShann had ballad singers.
Yeah, he had sometimes the men and sometimes the girls --
-- singers. But he didn't hardly fool any of them blues singers.
Well, it was kind of an -- almost an accident that you got sort of pushed into this blues thing so much.
